e.title: lost_years：把死亡率换算成「损失年数」，并接入 SSA、HLD 与 WHO 生命表
e.title_en: lost_years: converting mortality rates into expected years lost, joined to SSA, HLD and WHO life tables
e.title_hk: lost_years：把死亡率換算成「損失年數」，並接入 SSA、HLD 與 WHO 生命表
e.summary: 一个 Python 包（PyPI 发布）：把「死亡率」换算成更易理解的「预期损失年数」，并提供便捷方式接入美国社会安全署（SSA）精算数据、国际人类死亡率数据库（HLD）与 WHO 全球数据；部分生命表不随包分发，需另行安装，并使用规则见 README 的 Matching rules 一节
e.summary_en: A Python package published on PyPI that converts a mortality rate into the more interpretable expected number of years lost, and provides a convenient way to join US Social Security Administration actuarial data, international Human Life Database tables and WHO global data; some tables are not shipped with the package and must be installed separately, and matching rules are set out in the README
e.body:
**lost_years** 是一个**把死亡率换算成「预期损失年数」并接入多套官方生命表的 Python 包**（仓库 `gojiplus/lost-years`），**MIT 许可，实测 ★8、fork 数据未取、主语言 Python、仓库体量 3,050 KB、创建于 2020-04-02、最后推送 2026-09-08**（**均 GitHub API 实测值，在解冻窗口内**）；**其 topics 逐字实测为 coronavirus、covid-19、hld、life-tables、mortality、ssa、who**；**README 实测 16,927 字节**，**并实测带 PyPI 版本徽章、文档（GitHub Pages）徽章与下载量徽章**，**即该包已在 PyPI 正式发布**。

可核实信息（**均 README 逐字实测**）：**其标题逐字为「Lost Years: Expected Number of Years Lost」**；⭐⭐ **开篇一段逐字，是本条目最有价值的一句**：**「Mortality rate is puzzling to mortals. A better number is the expected number of years lost. (A yet better number would be quality-adjusted years lost.)」**——**「死亡率对凡人来说是费解的。一个更好的数字是**预期损失年数**。（更好的数字则是**质量调整后的损失年数**。）」**；**并逐字说明其用途**：**「To make it easier to calculate the expected years lost, `lost_years` provides a convenient way to join to the SSA actuarial data」**——**为便于计算预期损失年数，该包提供便捷方式接入 **SSA（美国社会安全署）精算数据****。⭐ **其数据来源在 README 中逐字分为三条路径**：**① 「US data (SSA)」——美国数据**；**② 「International data (HLD)」——国际数据（HLD，人类死亡率数据库）**；**③ 「Global data (WHO)」——全球数据（WHO）**；⭐ **并逐字提示其中一部分**不随包分发、需另行安装**：**「Install the tables that are not shipped (HLD, WHO)」**。**章节结构逐字实测**：**Matching rules／Application／Installation／Using lost_years／Command Line Interface／（三条数据路径）／As an External Library／As an External Library with Pandas DataFrame／Documentation／Authors／Contributor Code of Conduct／License**；⭐ **即它同时提供**命令行接口**与**作为库（含 Pandas DataFrame 用法）**两种用法，**且单设 `Matching rules` 一节说明匹配规则**。

对 RIAA：**① ⭐⭐⭐ 「死亡率对凡人来说是费解的。一个更好的数字是预期损失年数」是本条目最有价值的一句话，也是一个真正的沟通问题**——**死亡率（如每十万人 1,200）对非专业读者几乎不产生直觉**，**而「平均损失多少年」是任何人都能理解的量**；**对要向客户、管理层或公众解释死亡风险的保险与精算从业者，这正是一个可用的换算**；**可与池内 [[human-mortality-db]]、[[hmdhfdplus]]、[[mortalitytables]] 并读——**那几条提供**死亡率数据本身**，本条目提供的是**把它换成另一种单位**这一步****（**⚠️ 本次未运行该包，故不转述其交换算式的具体形式**）。**② ⭐⭐ 「质量调整后的损失年数（quality-adjusted years lost）」被括号特别提及，说明作者知道这一量的**更完整形式****——**即 `lost_years` 算的是**未调整**的损失年数**，**而作者明说还有一个更好的数字**（**⚠️ 本词条**不主张**该包实现了质量调整功能**——**README 原文只说「一个更好的数字会是……」，**本次未核实其是否提供该功能**）。**③ ⭐⭐ 「SSA 精算数据」这一接入对象值得注意**——**美国社会安全署（SSA）的**精算生命表**是美国官方死亡率基准之一**，**在养老金与社会保障测算中被广泛使用**；**对做年金、长寿风险或公共养老金的学生，这是一个**官方基准的便捷入口****（**⚠️ 本次未核实其取用的是 SSA 的哪一套表、哪一年版本**）。**④ ⭐⭐ 「三条数据路径（SSA／HLD／WHO）」把**辖区层次**讲清楚了**——**一国官方（美国）、跨国学术数据库（HLD）、全球汇总（WHO）**；**对做跨辖区死亡率比较的学生，这三级来源的**口径差异**是必须先处理的问题**（**⚠️ 本词条不主张三者的口径可比**）。**⑤ ⭐ 「部分生命表不随包分发、需另行安装」是一条**诚实的分发限制说明****——**HLD 与 WHO 的数据有其自身的授权与访问条件**，**故不能随包捆绑**；**这与第 319 轮 [[powmcp-skills]] 的「依赖披露」、第 320 轮 [[condition-parametric-zk]] 类的边界声明同属一种做法：**把「我为什么不能自带这个」说清楚****（**⚠️ 本次未核实 HLD／WHO 数据的具体授权条款**）。**⑥ ⭐ 「Matching rules（匹配规则）」单设一节**——**把死亡率表与目标人群匹配是有实际陷阱的**（**年龄分组边界、性别、年份、人口基数**），**单列一节说明是恰当的**（**本次未读该节正文，故不转述其规则**）。**⑦ ⭐ MIT 许可 ＋ PyPI 发布 ＋ 文档站点 ＋ 贡献者行为准则**，**说明其工程与社区规范程度较高**（**⚠️ 本次未访问其文档站点或 PyPI 页面**）。**⑧ ⭐ 该项目创建于 2020 年 4 月、topics 含 coronavirus／covid-19**，**即其起源与新冠期间「损失年数」这一指标受到广泛关注有关**——**可与池内 [[excessmort]]、[[rki-excess-mortality]] 并读：**三者都在处理「疫情/超额死亡如何量化」这一问题，而路径不同（方法包／官方数据／单位换算）****。

⚠️ **如实标注**：**①** 本次核实的是**仓库元数据、topics 七项、README（16,927 字节）的标题、开篇两段、三条数据路径名、章节结构，以及徽章所显示的 PyPI／文档／下载量入口的存在**，⭐ **但**未安装该包、未运行任何命令、未访问 PyPI 或文档站点、未打开 `Matching rules` 与其余章节正文、未查看其源码****，因此**不能转述其交换算式的具体形式、匹配规则、命令行参数、依赖关系、版本号、覆盖的年龄/性别/年份范围或任何计算结果**；**② ⭐⭐ 「死亡率换算成损失年数」这一功能与算式为**README 自述**，**本次未独立验证其数学正确性**；**③ ⭐⭐ **未核实该包是否实现了「质量调整后的损失年数」**——**本词条仅转述 README 提到这一概念更完整，**不主张该包已实现**；**④ ⭐ 「接入 SSA 精算数据」为**README 自述**，**未核实其实际取用的表种、年份版本与访问方式**（**SSA 数据的公开性与其使用条款亦未核实**）；**⑤ ⭐ 「部分生命表不随包分发（HLD、WHO）」为**README 自述**，**其具体原因（授权、体量或访问条件）本次未核实**；**⑥ ⭐ 本词条**不主张**该包适用于任何精算定价、准备金或养老金测算**——**一个单位换算工具有用，但距离可用于业务测算的死亡率假设仍有距离**；**⑦ ⭐ 本次未取该仓库的 fork 数（API 字段未读取）**，**故空置不填、不作推测**；**⑧ ⭐ 「死亡率对凡人来说是费解的」属**作者的主观表述**，**本词条引用它是因为它道出了真实的沟通问题，**不代表本词条对读者能力的判断**；**⑨ 是否有中文材料本次未核实**。**核实说明**：`https://api.github.com/repos/gojiplus/lost-years` 与 `/readme` 于 2026-09-11 经 GitHub API 实测读取（README 16,927 字节，标题、开篇与章节结构逐字核对）；**未安装、未运行、未访问 PyPI 与文档站点、未读 README 其余章节**。

e.body_en:
**lost_years** is a **Python package that converts a mortality rate into the expected number of years lost and joins to several official life tables** (repository `gojiplus/lost-years`), **MIT licensed, with measured ★8, Python as the primary language, a 3,050 KB repository, created 2020-04-02 and last pushed 2026-09-08** (**all GitHub API measurements, inside the thaw window**); **its topics measurably read coronavirus, covid-19, hld, life-tables, mortality, ssa and who**; **the README measures 16,927 bytes**, **and measurably carries a PyPI version badge, a documentation (GitHub Pages) badge and a downloads badge** — **i.e. the package is formally published on PyPI**.

Verifiable details (**all read verbatim from the README**): its **title reads verbatim "Lost Years: Expected Number of Years Lost"**; ⭐⭐ **the opening passage, verbatim, is the entry’s most valuable line**: **"Mortality rate is puzzling to mortals. A better number is the expected number of years lost. (A yet better number would be quality-adjusted years lost.)"**; **and its purpose, verbatim**: **"To make it easier to calculate the expected years lost, `lost_years` provides a convenient way to join to the SSA actuarial data"** — **a convenient way to join US Social Security Administration actuarial data**. ⭐ **Its data sources are named verbatim as three routes**: **① "US data (SSA)"**; **② "International data (HLD)"** (the Human Mortality Database); **③ "Global data (WHO)"**; ⭐ **and it states verbatim that some tables are not shipped and must be installed separately**: **"Install the tables that are not shipped (HLD, WHO)"**. **Section headings read verbatim**: **Matching rules / Application / Installation / Using lost_years / Command Line Interface / (the three data routes) / As an External Library / As an External Library with Pandas DataFrame / Documentation / Authors / Contributor Code of Conduct / License**; ⭐ **so it offers both a command-line interface and library use including a Pandas DataFrame route, and devotes a separate section to matching rules**.

For RIAA: **① ⭐⭐⭐ "Mortality rate is puzzling to mortals. A better number is the expected number of years lost" is the entry’s most valuable line and a real communication problem** — **a mortality rate (say 1,200 per 100,000) gives a lay reader almost no intuition**, **whereas "how many years are lost on average" is a quantity anyone grasps**; **for insurance and actuarial practitioners explaining death risk to clients, management or the public, this is a usable conversion**; **readable with [[human-mortality-db]], [[hmdhfdplus]] and [[mortalitytables]] — those supply the mortality data itself, whereas this supplies the step of restating it in another unit** (**⚠️ the package was not run, so the exact conversion formula is not restated**). **② ⭐⭐ "Quality-adjusted years lost" is mentioned in parenthesis, showing the author knows the fuller form of the quantity** — **i.e. `lost_years` calculates unadjusted years lost, and the author states outright that a better number exists** (**⚠️ the entry does not claim the package implements quality adjustment — the README only says a better number would be such, and whether it is implemented was not verified**). **③ ⭐⭐ The SSA actuarial data join is notable** — **the US Social Security Administration’s actuarial life tables are one of the official US mortality benchmarks**, **widely used in pension and social security projections**; **for students of annuities, longevity risk or public pensions, a convenient entry point to an official benchmark** (**⚠️ which SSA table and which year’s version it uses was not verified**). **④ ⭐⭐ The three data routes (SSA/HLD/WHO) make the jurisdictional layering clear** — **a national official source (US), a cross-national academic database (HLD) and a global aggregate (WHO)**; **for cross-jurisdiction mortality comparisons, the definitional differences among these three levels must be handled first** (**⚠️ the entry does not claim the three are comparable**). **⑤ ⭐ "Some tables are not shipped and must be installed separately" is an honest distribution limitation** — **HLD and WHO data carry their own licensing and access conditions**, **so they cannot be bundled**; **the same family as round 319’s [[powmcp-skills]] dependency disclosure and the contract-generation statement in [[condition-parametric-zk]]: state clearly why something cannot be included** (**⚠️ the specific terms for HLD and WHO data were not verified**). **⑥ ⭐ A separate "Matching rules" section** — **matching a mortality table to a target population has real pitfalls (age-band boundaries, sex, year, population base)**, **and giving them their own section is appropriate** (**that section’s body was not read, so its rules are not restated**). **⑦ ⭐ MIT licence plus PyPI publication plus a documentation site plus a contributor code of conduct** indicate **more engineering and community discipline than most projects of this size** (**⚠️ its documentation site and PyPI page were not visited**). **⑧ ⭐ The project was created in April 2020 with coronavirus and covid-19 among its topics**, **linking its origin to the period when "years lost" attracted wide attention during COVID-19** — **readable with [[excessmort]] and [[rki-excess-mortality]]: all three address how to quantify a pandemic or excess deaths, by different routes (methods package, official data, unit conversion)**.

⚠️ **Stated plainly**: **①** this check verified **the repository metadata, seven topics, and the README’s 16,927 bytes in respect of its title, opening passage, three data-route names and section structure, plus the existence of the PyPI, documentation and downloads entry points shown by its badges**, ⭐ **but did not install the package, run any command, visit PyPI or the documentation site, read the "Matching rules" or other section bodies, or inspect its source**, so **its conversion formula, matching rules, command-line arguments, dependencies, version number, covered age/sex/year ranges and any computed result cannot be restated**; **② ⭐⭐ The conversion of mortality into years lost is a README self-description**, **and its mathematical correctness was not independently validated**; **③ ⭐⭐ Whether the package implements quality-adjusted years lost was not verified** — **the entry only reports that the README mentions the fuller concept and does not claim it is implemented**; **④ ⭐ "Joins to the SSA actuarial data" is a README self-description**, **and which table, which year’s version and how it is accessed were not verified** (**nor was the public availability of SSA data or its terms of use**); **⑤ ⭐ That some tables are not shipped (HLD, WHO) is a README self-description**, **and the specific reason (licensing, size or access conditions) was not verified**; **⑥ ⭐ The entry does not claim the package is suitable for actuarial pricing, reserving or pension projection** — **a useful unit converter is still some distance from mortality assumptions usable in business calculations**; **⑦ ⭐ The repository’s fork count was not retrieved in this check (the API field was not read)**, **so it is left blank rather than guessed**; **⑧ ⭐ "Mortality rate is puzzling to mortals" is the author’s subjective phrasing** — **the entry quotes it because it names a real communication problem, not as a judgement on readers**; **⑨ whether Chinese-language material exists was not verified**. **Verification note**: `https://api.github.com/repos/gojiplus/lost-years` and `/readme` were read via the GitHub API on 2026-09-11 (the 16,927-byte README with title, opening and section structure checked verbatim); **nothing installed or run, PyPI and the documentation site not visited, remaining README sections unread**.

可核實資訊（**均 README 逐字實測**）：**標題逐字「Lost Years: Expected Number of Years Lost」**；⭐⭐ **開篇一段逐字，是本條目最有價值的一句**：**「Mortality rate is puzzling to mortals. A better number is the expected number of years lost. (A yet better number would be quality-adjusted years lost.)」**——**「死亡率對凡人來說是費解的。一個更好的數字是**預期損失年數**。（更好的數字則是**質量調整後的損失年數**。）」**；**並逐字說明用途**：**「To make it easier to calculate the expected years lost, `lost_years` provides a convenient way to join to the SSA actuarial data」**——**接入 **SSA（美國社會安全署）精算數據****。⭐ **三條數據路徑逐字**：**①「US data (SSA)」②「International data (HLD)」③「Global data (WHO)」**；⭐ **並逐字提示部分**不隨包分發、需另行安裝**：**「Install the tables that are not shipped (HLD, WHO)」**。**章節結構逐字實測**：**Matching rules／Application／Installation／Using lost_years／Command Line Interface／（三條數據路徑）／As an External Library／As an External Library with Pandas DataFrame／Documentation／Authors／Contributor Code of Conduct／License**；⭐ **即同時提供**命令行接口**與**作為庫（含 Pandas DataFrame 用法）**，且單設 `Matching rules` 一節**。

對 RIAA：**① ⭐⭐⭐ 「死亡率對凡人來說是費解的。一個更好的數字是預期損失年數」是本條目最有價值的一句話**——**死亡率（如每十萬人 1,200）對非專業讀者幾乎不產生直覺，而「平均損失多少年」是任何人都能理解的量**（可與 [[human-mortality-db]]、[[hmdhfdplus]]、[[mortalitytables]] 並讀——**那幾條提供**死亡率數據本身**，本條目提供的是**把它換成另一種單位**這一步****；**⚠️ 未運行該包，故不轉述其換算式的具體形式**）。**② ⭐⭐ 「質量調整後的損失年數」被特別提及，說明作者知道這一量的**更完整形式****——**⚠️ 本詞條**不主張**該包實現了質量調整功能**。**③ ⭐⭐ 「SSA 精算數據」這一接入對象值得注意**——**美國社會安全署的精算生命表是美國官方死亡率基準之一，在養老金與社會保障測算中廣泛使用****（**⚠️ 未核實其取用的是哪一套表、哪一年版本**）。**④ ⭐⭐ 「三條數據路徑（SSA／HLD／WHO）」把**轄區層次**講清楚了**——**一國官方、跨國學術數據庫、全球匯總****（**⚠️ 不主張三者口徑可比**）。**⑤ ⭐ 「部分生命表不隨包分發、需另行安裝」是一條**誠實的分發限制說明****（與第 319 輪 [[powmcp-skills]]、第 320 輪 [[condition-parametric-zk]] 同屬一種做法）。**⑥ ⭐ 「Matching rules」單設一節**——**把死亡率表與目標人群匹配有實際陷阱**（**未讀該節正文，故不轉述其規則**）。**⑦ ⭐ MIT 許可 ＋ PyPI 發布 ＋ 文檔站點 ＋ 貢獻者行為準則**。**⑧ ⭐ 創建於 2020 年 4 月、topics 含 coronavirus／covid-19**（可與 [[excessmort]]、[[rki-excess-mortality]] 並讀——**三者都在處理「疫情/超額死亡如何量化」，而路徑不同**）。
